title: Kennedy Space Center Master Plan Digest — Phase 65 Florida Space Coast authority and mission delivery review
summary: Phase 65 reviews this primary record as part of the Florida Space Coast authority and mission delivery reporting pack. NASA's 2026 Kennedy Space Center master-plan digest frames long-range land, facilities, utilities, transportation, resilience, and multi-user development as a connected infrastructure system.
key_findings: The plan organizes Kennedy's future around a multi-user federal spaceport and shared infrastructure.
It identifies long-range land-use, facility, utility, transportation, environmental, and resilience considerations.
Plan inclusion does not establish appropriation, project authorization, design, procurement, construction, acceptance, or use.
why_it_matters: Which records connect licences, operators, infrastructure capital, construction, accepted facilities, mission use, safety, and repeat operations? This record supplies one bounded part of that evidence chain; it is not a substitute for the pack's downstream records. The plan supplies the Space Coast system envelope against which named capital, license, construction, and mission records can be tested.
ftfn_relevance: Anchors the Florida planning and infrastructure layer.
Connects launch activity to shared utilities, land, transportation, resilience, and institutional authority.
Creates a path from long-range plan elements to funded and accepted projects.
evidence_limits: Inclusion in a Phase 65 reporting pack does not advance a Phase 64 matrix cell or establish an operating outcome.
A master plan is not an appropriated capital program.
Named concepts are not completed designs, contracts, or built assets.
The record does not establish site utilization, mission licensing, cadence, safety, or economic outcomes.
